## Artistry

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=King_Diamond&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Artistry")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/49/King_Diamond_Rockharz_2025_17.jpg/250px-King_Diamond_Rockharz_2025_17.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:King_Diamond_Rockharz_2025_17.jpg)

Diamond performing in Ballenstedt, Germany in 2025

Diamond is known for his multi-octave vocal range, in particular his far reaching and stable tone when singing in [falsetto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falsetto "Falsetto").[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-41)[_Revolver_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Revolver_(magazine) "Revolver (magazine)") wrote "the Danish metal royal has commanded our attention through Satan-summoning performances, demonic grunting and a glass-shattering falsetto that’s part [Maria Callas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maria_Callas "Maria Callas"), part [Rob Halford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rob_Halford "Rob Halford") and completely jaw-dropping."[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-42)

He is known for creating conceptual works that feature recurring stories that include the supernatural, horror, fate and death. His lyrics have been described as a "gothic horror romance in metal form, delivered with technical precision and theatrical grandeur."[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:1-38) Diamond has stated he has loved of [horror films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horror_film "Horror film") since his youth when he would watch _[Frankenstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frankenstein\_(1931\_film) "Frankenstein (1931 film)")_ and _[Dracula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dracula\_(1958\_film) "Dracula (1958 film)")_ with his parents; these films have also played a part in his lyrical style.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:2-7) Diamond said that when he first joined [Mercyful Fate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate "Mercyful Fate"), he lived in a apartment that "turned out to be truly haunted." He stated in an interview with [Blabbermouth.net](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blabbermouth.net "Blabbermouth.net"): "Many of the things that are written in the lyrics have been taken straight as they happened from these real experiences."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:2-7) In that same interview, he stated that a lot of his lyrics are drawn from real life, but some come from his imagination: "To make a story flow, you change some of the things that you've experienced. When an album is done and I read through all the lyrics, I get a little uneasy when I see how much of myself I've put into the stories. But then again, I know that no one's going to know unless I tell them exactly what's what, and I'm certainly not going to do that. But it's drawn from everywhere."[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:2-7)

Diamond cites [Arthur Brown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthur_Brown_(musician) "Arthur Brown (musician)"), [David Byron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Byron "David Byron"), [Alice Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alice_Cooper "Alice Cooper"), [Ronnie James Dio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronnie_James_Dio "Ronnie James Dio"), [Ian Gillan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Gillan "Ian Gillan"), [Ozzy Osbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ozzy_Osbourne "Ozzy Osbourne") and [Robert Plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Plant "Robert Plant") as his primary influences. According to Diamond's biography on his official website, the first two albums he bought were [Deep Purple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_Purple "Deep Purple")'s _[Fireball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fireball\_(album) "Fireball (album)")_ and [Black Sabbath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Sabbath "Black Sabbath")'s _[Master of Reality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master\_of\_Reality "Master of Reality")_.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-43)

### Stage presence

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=King_Diamond&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Stage presence")]

On stage, Diamond uses a microphone stand consisting of a [femur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femur "Femur") bone and a [tibia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tibia "Tibia") bone in the shape of a [cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross "Cross"). He previously used a [human skull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_skull "Human skull"), called Melissa, on stage. In the mid-1980s Melissa was stolen after a performance in the Netherlands.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Diamond is also known for his [Corpse paint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corpse_paint "Corpse paint") and has changed the design of his make-up often over the years. With _[Conspiracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conspiracy\_(King\_Diamond\_album) "Conspiracy (King Diamond album)")_, he wore a mesh of black and white line war paint, with some red "blood" made to look like a wound coming out of his forehead. With his album _[The Puppet Master](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Puppet\_Master\_(album) "The Puppet Master (album)")_, he used very little white and mainly had black crosses and inverted crosses going up and down his face.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-44) Diamond is also known for his onstage performance. _Brave Worlds_ described his stage presence stating "On stage, he transforms the concert into a dark theatre – a ritual where gothic tales, horrific characters and symbolic scenography merge. His distinctive "corpsepaint" and his microphone holder, an inverted cross made of human bones, make him an iconic figure."[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:1-38)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=King_Diamond&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Personal life")]

Diamond is married to [Livia Zita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Livia_Zita "Livia Zita"), a Hungarian-born singer who has made appearances as a backup vocalist on the albums _[The Puppet Master](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Puppet\_Master\_(album) "The Puppet Master (album)")_ and _[Give Me Your Soul...Please](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Give\_Me\_Your\_Soul...Please "Give Me Your Soul...Please")_, as well as during live performances. She is also his business partner, and is currently[_[when?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual\_of\_Style/Dates\_and\_numbers#Chronological\_items "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")_] working with him to compile old footage for two planned DVD releases of King Diamond and Mercyful Fate live performances. She also helped him make remastered editions of the King Diamond albums _[The Spider's Lullabye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Spider's\_Lullabye "The Spider's Lullabye")_, _[The Graveyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Graveyard\_(album) "The Graveyard (album)")_, _[Voodoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voodoo\_(King\_Diamond\_album) "Voodoo (King Diamond album)")_ and _[House of God](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House\_of\_God\_(album) "House of God (album)")_.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-45) In 2017, they became parents to a son,[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-46) born in March.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-48) In a 2016 interview with _[Metal Hammer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metal\_Hammer "Metal Hammer")_ Diamond revealed that following his health scare he has given up smoking and started living a healthier life style, which he has credited to helping improve his singing voice.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:3-49) Some of Diamonds interest include [Formula One](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_One "Formula One") and [Football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football"), growing up he played for the youth squad of Danish club called [Hvidovre IF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hvidovre_IF "Hvidovre IF") but he stopped playing once he went to college and started getting involved in music.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:3-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-50)

Although he was born and raised in Denmark, Diamond relocated to [Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas "Dallas") / [Fort Worth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fort_Worth,_Texas "Fort Worth, Texas"), [Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas "Texas") in the 1980s.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-51) In 2010, Diamond officially quit smoking following his [triple-bypass-surgery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coronary_artery_bypass_surgery "Coronary artery bypass surgery").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:3-49)

Diamond follows[LaVeyan Satanism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LaVeyan_Satanism "LaVeyan Satanism"), which he does not see as a [religion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Religion "Religion"), but a [philosophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philosophy "Philosophy") by which he lived even before reading [occultist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occult "Occult")[Anton LaVey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anton_LaVey "Anton LaVey")'s _[The Satanic Bible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Satanic\_Bible "The Satanic Bible")_.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-rhi1-52)[Michael Moynihan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Jenkins_Moynihan "Michael Jenkins Moynihan") calls him "one of the only performers of the '80s Satanic Metal who was more than just a [poseur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poseur "Poseur") using a devilish image for [shock value](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shock_value "Shock value")".[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-loc15f-53) Diamond has expressed concern that religion has led so many people to kill and destroy each other. He stated that he cannot comprehend why religion has caused so much death and destruction when it is logically impossible to prove the presence or absence of any [deity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deity "Deity"). He states that he has reached a point in his life where he has completely given up believing in anything religious.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-54) Despite being non religious Diamond revealed in a 2016, interview with _[Metal Hammer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metal\_Hammer "Metal Hammer")_ that he is "very [spiritual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spirituality "Spirituality")."[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-:3-49)

## Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=King_Diamond&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Legacy")]

Metallica released an 11-minute medley of five Mercyful Fate songs on their 1998 _[Garage Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garage\_Inc. "Garage Inc.")_ cover album. King Diamond has provided guest vocals for live performances of the medley at Metallica's concerts on three occasions: at the 1999 [Gods of Metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gods_of_Metal "Gods of Metal") festival in [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milan "Milan"), Italy (with Hank Shermann on guitar);[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-55) at the 2008 [Ozzfest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ozzfest "Ozzfest") in [Dallas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dallas "Dallas"), Texas;[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-56) and at a 2011 Metallica fan club gig in [San Francisco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco "San Francisco"), California (with Hank Shermann on guitar, Michael Denner on guitar and Timi Hansen on bass).[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-GWorld-57)

King Diamond has appeared on the covers of many rock and metal magazines, and has influenced many artists, including Metallica's [Lars Ulrich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lars_Ulrich "Lars Ulrich"),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-auto-3)[Cradle of Filth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cradle_of_Filth "Cradle of Filth"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-auto1-5)[Cage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cage_(band) "Cage (band)"),[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-58) and [Andy DiGelsomina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_DiGelsomina "Andy DiGelsomina") of the Wagnerian opera metal project [Lyraka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyraka "Lyraka").[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-59)

American heavy metal band Cage devoted to him the song "King Diamond" on the album _[Hell Destroyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hell\_Destroyer "Hell Destroyer")_ in 2007.

In 2006, Diamond was ranked at number 85 in _[Hit Parader](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hit\_Parader "Hit Parader")'s_ "Top 100 Metal Vocalists of All Time".[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-60) In 2016 he was ranked number 38 on _[Loudwire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loudwire "Loudwire")_’s list of the 66 Best Hard Rock and Metal Frontman of All Time.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-61)

King Diamond has inspired many bands; [Metallica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metallica "Metallica"),[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-62)[Slayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slayer "Slayer"),[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-63)[Opeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opeth "Opeth"),[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-64)[Pantera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pantera "Pantera"),[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-65)[Cradle of Filth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cradle_of_Filth "Cradle of Filth")[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-auto1-5) and [Emperor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emperor_(Norwegian_band) "Emperor (Norwegian band)")[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond#cite_note-66) have all cited him as a influence.

**King Diamond** is a Danish [heavy metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavy_metal_music "Heavy metal music") band formed in 1985 by vocalist [King Diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond "King Diamond"), guitarists [Andy LaRocque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_LaRocque "Andy LaRocque") and Michael Denner, bassist [Timi Hansen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timi_Hansen "Timi Hansen"), and drummer [Mikkey Dee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikkey_Dee "Mikkey Dee"). King, Denner and Hansen had recently disbanded [Mercyful Fate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate "Mercyful Fate"), and formed a new band under the King Diamond moniker, already known from the initial Mercyful Fate era.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-YouTube_#1-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Music_Box-2) Since the band's inception, there have been over fifteen musicians in and out of King Diamond, with Diamond as the only remaining original member, while LaRocque remained until 2026. Their current line-up consists of Diamond, guitarist [Mike Wead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Wead "Mike Wead"), drummer Matt Thompson, bassist Pontus Egberg and guitarist [Gus G](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gus_G "Gus G") as LaRocque's replacement.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Band_members-4)

King Diamond has released twelve [studio albums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studio_album "Studio album") (most of them [concept albums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concept_album "Concept album")), two [live albums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_album "Live album"), two [extended plays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extended_play "Extended play"), five [compilation albums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compilation_album "Compilation album"), and five [singles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single_(music) "Single (music)"). Their first album, _[Fatal Portrait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatal\_Portrait "Fatal Portrait")_, was released in 1986, followed a year later by the band's first concept album, _[Abigail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abigail\_(album) "Abigail (album)")_ (1987). Three more albums followed – _["Them"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them\_(King\_Diamond\_album) "Them (King Diamond album)")_ (1988), _[Conspiracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conspiracy\_(King\_Diamond\_album) "Conspiracy (King Diamond album)")_ (1989), and _[The Eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Eye\_(King\_Diamond\_album) "The Eye (King Diamond album)")_ (1990) – before the band went on hiatus around 1992, when King Diamond, Denner, and Hansen reformed Mercyful Fate.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Band_members-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Allmusic-5) He reformed the King Diamond band in 1994, and balanced recording and touring with Mercyful Fate and his eponymous band for nearly a decade, until the former went on hiatus again by the early 2000s. King Diamond's studio output has been minimal since 2007's _[Give Me Your Soul...Please](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Give\_Me\_Your\_Soul...Please "Give Me Your Soul...Please")_, though the band has continued to perform live and occasionally teased more than one upcoming album.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Spider_Lily-6)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=King_Diamond_(band)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Formation, _Fatal Portrait_ and _Abigail_ (1985–1987)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=King_Diamond_(band)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Formation, Fatal Portrait and Abigail (1985–1987)")]

Vocalist [King Diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond "King Diamond"), guitarist Michael Denner, and bassist [Timi Hansen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timi_Hansen "Timi Hansen") formed the band in 1985.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-YouTube_#1-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Music_Box-2) The three had recently departed [Mercyful Fate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate "Mercyful Fate") due to musical differences between Diamond and guitarist [Hank Shermann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hank_Shermann "Hank Shermann").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-YouTube_#1-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Music_Box-2)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Allmusic-5) According to Diamond, when he, Denner, and Hansen formed a new band, they chose the name "King Diamond" to "get better deals", and because the name was already known from Mercyful Fate.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-YouTube_#1-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Music_Box-2) To round out the line-up, the group hired Swedish musicians [Mikkey Dee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mikkey_Dee "Mikkey Dee") on drums and guitarist Floyd Konstantin, the latter of whom was dismissed two weeks before recording the debut album,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-7) and replaced by Swedish musician [Andy LaRocque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_LaRocque "Andy LaRocque").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Band_members-4)

In July 1985, the band began recording their debut album at Sound Track Studio in [Copenhagen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copenhagen "Copenhagen").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Fatal_Portrait-8) On 25 December, they released debut single "No Presents for Christmas".[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-No_Presents_for_Christmas-9)_[Fatal Portrait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatal\_Portrait "Fatal Portrait")_, the band's first full-length studio album, was released on 14 March 1986,[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-10) through [Roadrunner Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roadrunner_Records "Roadrunner Records").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Fatal_Portrait-8) Produced by Rune Höyer and Diamond, the album charted at number 33 on the Swedish album chart,[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Fatal_SWE-11) and spawned the single "Halloween", released on 6 June 1986.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Halloween-12)

In December 1986, King Diamond began recording their second studio album at Sound Track Studio in Copenhagen.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Abigail-13)_[Abigail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abigail\_(album) "Abigail (album)")_ was released on 29 May 1987,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-14) and is the first [concept album](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Concept_album "Concept album") based on an original story by Diamond.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Abigail-13)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-YouTube_#2-15) The album was supported by its sole single, "The Family Ghost", for which they shot their first music video,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-The_Family_Ghost-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-The_Family_Ghost_music_video-17) and it went on to chart at number 39 in Sweden,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Abigail_SWE-18) number 68 in the Netherlands,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Abigail_SWE-18) and at number 123 on the [_Billboard_ 200](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_200 "Billboard 200").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Abigail_Billboard-19) Following _Abigail_'s release, Denner left the band due to touring strains.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-YouTube_#2-15) He was replaced by [Mike Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Moon_(musician) "Mike Moon (musician)") for the album's supporting tour, during which the band recorded the live album _[In Concert 1987: Abigail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In\_Concert\_1987:\_Abigail "In Concert 1987: Abigail")_, officially released until 1991.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Band_members-4)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Abigail_Live-20)

### _"Them"_ and _Conspiracy_ (1988–1989)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=King_Diamond_(band)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: \"Them\" and Conspiracy (1988–1989)")]

Following the _Abigail_ tour, Moon and Timi Hansen were replaced by Pete Blakk and Hal Patino, respectively.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Band_members-4) On 18 July 1988, King Diamond released _["Them"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Them\_(King\_Diamond\_album) "Them (King Diamond album)")_, recorded at M.M.C. Studio in Copenhagen, Denmark.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Them-21) Another concept album, _"Them"_ charted at number 38 on the Swedish album chart,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Them_SWE-22) number 65 on the Dutch album chart,[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Them_SWE-22) and at number 89 on the _Billboard_ 200,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Them_Billboard-23) making it King Diamond's highest charting album in the U.S. to date. Another music video was shot, for the single "Welcome Home".[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Welcome_Home-24) On 1 November, the group released _[The Dark Sides](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Dark\_Sides "The Dark Sides")_ EP, a collection of previously released material and one unreleased track.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-The_Dark_Sides-25)

Following the tour for _"Them"_, Dee left King Diamond.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Band_members-4) He was rehired to play drums on the band's follow-up album, after which he was replaced by [Snowy Shaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snowy_Shaw "Snowy Shaw").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Band_members-4) On 21 August 1989, King Diamond released _[Conspiracy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conspiracy\_(King\_Diamond\_album) "Conspiracy (King Diamond album)")_, which charted at number 41 on the Swedish album chart,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Conspiracy_SWE-26) number 64 on the Dutch album chart,[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Conspiracy_SWE-26) and at number 111 on the _Billboard_ 200.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Conspiracy-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Conspiracy_Billboard-28) A continuation of the storyline from _"Them"_, _Conspiracy_ was the first King Diamond album recorded in the United States. It was tracked at [Rumbo Recording Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rumbo_Recorders "Rumbo Recorders") in [Canoga Park, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canoga_Park,_Los_Angeles "Canoga Park, Los Angeles"). A music video was made for the track "Sleepless Nights".[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Sleepless_Nights-29)

### _The Eye_ to _House of God_ (1990–2000)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=King_Diamond_(band)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: The Eye to House of God (1990–2000)")]

In June 1990, King Diamond began recording _[The Eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Eye\_(King\_Diamond\_album) "The Eye (King Diamond album)")_ at [Sweet Silence Studios](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweet_Silence_Studios "Sweet Silence Studios") in Copenhagen, Denmark. It was released on 30 October 1990.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-The_Eye-30) Shaw performed the drums on the album using [drum pads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electronic_drum "Electronic drum").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-31) It debuted at number 179 on the _Billboard_ 200.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-The_Eye-30)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-The_Eye_Billboard-32) The band did not tour in support of the album due to lack of label support. Following _The Eye_, Hal Patino and Pete Blakk were replaced by [Sharlee D'Angelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharlee_D'Angelo "Sharlee D'Angelo") and [Mike Wead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Wead "Mike Wead"), respectively.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Band_members-4)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Mercyful_Fate_Band_members-33) This line-up did not record any material, as Diamond reunited with Mercyful Fate in 1992. He would balance recording and touring with Mercyful Fate and his eponymous band for the remainder of the 1990s.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Band_members-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Allmusic-5)

After recording and touring with Mercyful Fate, King Diamond reformed in 1994.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Spider-34) With King Diamond, Andy La Rocque, as well as guitarist Herb Simonsen, bassist [Chris Estes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Estes "Chris Estes") and drummer Darrin Anthony from the Texas band Mindstorm, the band spent September through October 1994, recording their next album.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Band_members-4)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Spider-34) Released on 6 June 1995, _[The Spider's Lullabye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Spider's\_Lullabye "The Spider's Lullabye")_ was the band's first album on [Metal Blade Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metal_Blade_Records "Metal Blade Records"), and their first studio release since _Fatal Portrait_ to not be a concept album.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Spider-34) The album peaked at number 31 on the [Finnish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finland "Finland") album charts.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Spider_FIN-35) In March 1996, King Diamond began recording their seventh studio album at the Dallas Sound Lab.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Graveyard-36) King Diamond return to writing concept albums with _[The Graveyard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Graveyard\_(album) "The Graveyard (album)")_, released on 1 October 1996.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Graveyard-36) The album charted at number 23 in Finland.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Graveyard_FIN-37) After the album's release, drummer Darrin Anthony left the band due to a car accident and was replaced by former [Chastain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chastain_(band) "Chastain (band)") drummer John Luke Hebert.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Band_members-4)

On 24 February 1998, King Diamond released _[Voodoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voodoo\_(King\_Diamond\_album) "Voodoo (King Diamond album)")_, which charted at number 27 on the Finnish album chart[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Voodoo_FIN-38) and at number 55 on the Swedish album chart.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Voodoo_SWE-39) After the album's release, guitarist Herb Simonsen was replaced by [Glen Drover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glen_Drover "Glen Drover").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Band_members-4)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Voodoo-40) When Mercyful Fate was put on hold in 1999, King Diamond began recording _[House of God](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House\_of\_God\_(album) "House of God (album)")_ at the Nomad Recording Studio in [Carrollton, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrollton,_Texas "Carrollton, Texas"), with new bassist [Paul David Harbour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_David_Harbour "Paul David Harbour"), who had replaced Chris Estes.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-House_of_God-41) Released on 20 June 2000,[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-House_of_God-41) the album peaked at number 60 in Sweden.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-House_of_God_SWE-42) After the album's release, Drover, drummer Hebert and Harbour were replaced by Mike Wead, Matt Thompson and Hal Patino, respectively.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Band_members-4)

### Later years (2001–2017)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=King_Diamond_(band)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Later years (2001–2017)")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/a/a5/King_Diamond.jpg/250px-King_Diamond.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:King_Diamond.jpg)

King Diamond performing in [Kraków](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krak%C3%B3w "Kraków"), 2001

In May 2001, King Diamond began recording its tenth studio album at the Nomad Recording Studio.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Abigail_II-43) Released on 29 January 2002, _[Abigail II: The Revenge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abigail\_II:\_The\_Revenge "Abigail II: The Revenge")_ was a sequel to 1987's _Abigail_.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Abigail_II-43) It was the first King Diamond album since 1990's _The Eye_ to feature Patino, who rejoined the band during the recording process.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Band_members-4)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Abigail_II-43) King Diamond did not tour in support of _Abigail II_, as Metal Blade could not provide tour support, due to illegal downloading.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Metallian-44) Despite this, the album peaked at number 24 in Finland[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Abigail_II_FIN-45) and at number 42 in Sweden.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Abigail_II_SWE-46)

On 21 October 2003, King Diamond released _[The Puppet Master](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Puppet\_Master\_(album) "The Puppet Master (album)")_,[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Puppet_Master-47) which charted at number 36 in Sweden.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Puppet_Master_SWE-48) Besides the band, the album featured additional vocals from Diamond's wife [Livia Zita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Livia_Zita "Livia Zita").[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Puppet_Master-47) During the supporting tour for _The Puppet Master_, the band recorded the live album _[Deadly Lullabyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deadly\_Lullabyes "Deadly Lullabyes")_, released 21 September 2004.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Deadly_Lullabyes-49) In April 2006, Dee (currently with [Scorpions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scorpions_(band) "Scorpions (band)"), formerly with [Motörhead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mot%C3%B6rhead "Motörhead")) guestappeared at King Diamond's sold-out show in [Gothenburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gothenburg "Gothenburg"), Sweden.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-50) On 26 June 2007, King Diamond released _[Give Me Your Soul...Please](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Give\_Me\_Your\_Soul...Please "Give Me Your Soul...Please")_.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Give_Me_Your_Soul-51) The album peaked at number 25 on the Finnish chart,[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Give_Me_FIN-52) number 28 on the Swedish chart,[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Give_Me_SWE-53) and at number 174 on the _Billboard_ 200.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Give_Me_Billboard-54) The track "Never Ending Hill" was nominated for a [Grammy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Awards "Grammy Awards") for "[Best Metal Performance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Best_Metal_Performance "Grammy Award for Best Metal Performance")" (the group's first). A music video was made for the title track.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Give_Me_music_video-55)

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/King_Diamond_live_2006_Moscow_02.jpg/250px-King_Diamond_live_2006_Moscow_02.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:King_Diamond_live_2006_Moscow_02.jpg)

King Diamond (left) and [Andy LaRocque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_LaRocque "Andy LaRocque") (right) performing in [Moscow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moscow "Moscow"), 2006

In late November 2010, Diamond was hospitalized after having several heart attacks.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Artisan-56) It was discovered that three of his arteries were blocked. He underwent [triple bypass surgery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coronary_artery_bypass_surgery "Coronary artery bypass surgery").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Artisan-56) Following a successful operation, he returned home to rest.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Artisan-56) Diamond stopped smoking, changed his diet, and began exercising regularly, according to his wife.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Three_Songs-57) On 27 January 2012, Diamond made a special appearance at the "5th Annual Nomad Recording Studio Throwdown", performing three songs: "The Family Ghost", "Evil" and "Burn".[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Three_Songs-57) On 9 June 2012, the King Diamond band played at the [Sweden Rock Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sweden_Rock_Festival "Sweden Rock Festival").[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Sweden-58) They were joined on stage by Michael Denner, Hank Shermann, Mikkey Dee and [Volbeat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Volbeat "Volbeat")'s [Michael Poulsen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Poulsen "Michael Poulsen").[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Sweden-58) Diamond stated that the band was expected to begin writing their thirteenth studio album in the fall of 2012.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-2012_Interview-59)

On 19 July 2014, the band announced that Patino had been dismissed for reasons similar to his firing from King Diamond in 1990.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-60) He was replaced by Pontus Egberg, formerly of [Lion's Share](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lion's_Share_(band) "Lion's Share (band)") and [the Poodles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Poodles "The Poodles"). In October, King Diamond announced the compilation _Dreams of Horror_, released in November through Metal Blade Records, covering the band's career.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-61) In December, Egberg became an official member of the band.[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-62)

King Diamond took part in the 2015 Rockstar Energy Mayhem Festival along with headliner [Slayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slayer "Slayer"), [Hellyeah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hellyeah "Hellyeah"), [The Devil Wears Prada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Devil_Wears_Prada_(band) "The Devil Wears Prada (band)"), [Thy Art Is Murder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thy_Art_Is_Murder "Thy Art Is Murder"), [Jungle Rot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jungle_Rot "Jungle Rot"), [Sister Sin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sister_Sin "Sister Sin"), [Sworn In](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sworn_In_(band) "Sworn In (band)"), [Shattered Sun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shattered_Sun "Shattered Sun"), [Feed Her to the Sharks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feed_Her_to_the_Sharks "Feed Her to the Sharks"), [Code Orange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_Orange_(band) "Code Orange (band)") and Kissing Candice. The tour ran from 26 June through 2 August.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-63) At the 8 July 2015 show in [Milwaukee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milwaukee "Milwaukee"), [Wisconsin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wisconsin "Wisconsin"), Diamond perform without face paint due to an eye infection; doctors advised against makeup. He said that there was no negative feedback from the fans.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-64) The band embarked on a U.S. tour from October to December 2015 with [Exodus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exodus_(band) "Exodus (band)"), where they performed _Abigail_ in its entirety.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-65)

### _Saint Lucifer's Hospital 1920_ and planned future albums (2018–present)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=King_Diamond_(band)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Saint Lucifer's Hospital 1920 and planned future albums (2018–present)")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/05/King_Diamond_Rockharz_2025_20.jpg/250px-King_Diamond_Rockharz_2025_20.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:King_Diamond_Rockharz_2025_20.jpg)

King Diamond performing in Ballenstedt, Germany, 2025

By 2018, King Diamond had begun work on its thirteenth studio album,[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-66) divided into two parts to connect with its theme.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-67) The first part of the series was revealed to be titled _The Institute_; the title was changed to _Saint Lucifer's Hospital 1920_.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-68) The album has been delayed many times since its initial planned release date of 2020,[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-69)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-70)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-71) due to frontman [King Diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond "King Diamond") taking his time on perfecting new material by the King Diamond band and the reunited [Mercyful Fate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate "Mercyful Fate").[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-72)[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-73)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-74) The first single from the album, "Masquerade of Madness", was available for streaming on 8 November 2019.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-75) On 25 January 2019, the band's first live DVD/Blu-ray, _Songs for the Dead Live_, was released.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-76) The band embarked on a North American tour with [Uncle Acid and the Deadbeats](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uncle_Acid_&_the_Deadbeats "Uncle Acid & the Deadbeats") and [Idle Hands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unto_Others_(band) "Unto Others (band)").[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-77)

On 15 October 2024, during a performance at the [Port Authority of San Antonio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Port_San_Antonio "Port San Antonio"), King Diamond debuted the songs "Spider Lilly" and "Electro Therapy".[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-78) On this tour, which was supported by [Overkill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overkill_(band) "Overkill (band)") and [Night Demon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Night_Demon_(band) "Night Demon (band)"),[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-79) the band was joined by [Myrkur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myrkur "Myrkur") on keyboards,[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-80) and she appears on the studio recording of "Spider Lilly", released as a single on 17 December.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-81) It was also the debut single from the band's forthcoming "Horror Trilogy", with the first part titled _Saint Lucifer's Hospital 1920_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-Spider_Lily-6) During the summer of 2025, King Diamond went on a European tour; some dates were cancelled due to Diamond having [strep throat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Streptococcal_pharyngitis "Streptococcal pharyngitis").[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-82)

In November 2025, Diamond was honored by the [Danish Arts Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danish_Arts_Foundation "Danish Arts Foundation") and given the lifetime honour for his "very special efforts and contributions to Danish art and cultural life." In addition, Diamond will receive a yearly 189,000 Danish Kroner (about $26,000) grant from the foundation for the rest of his life.[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-:0-83)[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-84)

In March 2026, guitarist [Andy LaRocque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_LaRocque "Andy LaRocque") stated that the band was hoping to release their 13th studio album _Saint Lucifer's Hospital 1920_ sometime later in the year.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-85) When asked that June when it would be released, LaRocque admitted, "Nobody knows. We'll see. But all I can say is that we're working on it."[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-86)

On 24 July 2026, it was announced that the band had parted ways with original guitarist [Andy LaRocque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andy_LaRocque "Andy LaRocque"), and was replaced by [Firewind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Firewind "Firewind") and former [Ozzy Osbourne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ozzy_Osbourne "Ozzy Osbourne") guitarist [Gus G](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gus_G "Gus G").[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-87) King Diamond confirmed that September that the band's new album will be released in 2028.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-88)

## Artistry

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=King_Diamond_(band)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Artistry")]

Although King Diamond is primarily a [heavy metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavy_metal_music "Heavy metal music") or [extreme metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extreme_metal "Extreme metal") band,[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-89)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-90)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-91) their works have seen the band combine elements of [thrash metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrash_metal "Thrash metal"),[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-powerofprog-92)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-93)[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-metalinvader-94)[speed metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Speed_metal "Speed metal"),[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-powerofprog-92)[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-revolver_2017-95)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-bravewords_2025-96)[black metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_metal "Black metal"),[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-powerofprog-92)[power metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Power_metal "Power metal"),[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-revolver_2017-95)[progressive metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_metal "Progressive metal"),[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-metalinvader-94)[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-97) and [groove metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groove_metal "Groove metal"),[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-bravewords_2025-96) with "spectacular spooky heavy metal" and "theatrical storytelling".[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-metalinvader-94)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-bravewords_2025-96)

Lyrically, King Diamond is known for creating conceptual works that feature recurring stories that include the supernatural, horror, fate and death. His lyrics have been described as a "gothic horror romance in metal form, delivered with technical precision and theatrical grandeur."[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-:0-83) In an interview with _[Blabbermouth.net](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blabbermouth.net "Blabbermouth.net")_, Diamond stated that a lot of his lyrics are drawn from real-life, but some comes from his imagination "to make a story flow, you change some of the things that you've experienced. When an album is done and I read through all the lyrics, I get a little uneasy when I see how much of myself I've put into the stories. But then again, I know that no one's going to know unless I tell them exactly what's what, and I'm certainly not going to do that. But it's drawn from everywhere."[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-98)

The band is known for their massive production during live performances featuring fog in order to create creepy on stage theatrics.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-99) Their lead singer King Diamond is also known to use a microphone stand consisting of a [femur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femur "Femur") bone and a [tibia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tibia "Tibia") bone in the shape of a [cross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cross "Cross"), while also dawning his signature [Corpse paint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corpse_paint "Corpse paint"). _[CBS News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS\_News "CBS News")_ described him as a "menacing figure live".[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-100)[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band)#cite_note-101)
