**Mercyful Fate** is a Danish [heavy metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavy_metal_music "Heavy metal music") band from [Copenhagen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copenhagen "Copenhagen"), formed in 1981 by vocalist [King Diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond "King Diamond") and guitarist [Hank Shermann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hank_Shermann "Hank Shermann").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-shermann_bio-2) Influenced by [progressive rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_rock "Progressive rock") and [hard rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_rock "Hard rock"), and with lyrics dealing with [LaVeyan Satanism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LaVeyan_Satanism "LaVeyan Satanism") (often with [ironic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irony "Irony") or [sardonic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sardonicism "Sardonicism") use of [Christian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christianity "Christianity") themes) and the [occult](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occult "Occult"), Mercyful Fate was part of the [first wave of black metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First-wave_black_metal "First-wave black metal") in the early to mid-1980s, along with [Venom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venom_(band) "Venom (band)") and [Bathory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bathory_(band) "Bathory (band)").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-4) The band is also cited as a formative influence to the then-nascent genres of [thrash metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrash_metal "Thrash metal")[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Kerry_King-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-metalinjection-6) and [death metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_metal "Death metal"), as well as the [Norwegian black metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Music_of_Norway#Black_metal "Music of Norway") scene.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Melissa_Review-9)

Since its inception in 1981, Mercyful Fate has released seven studio albums, two [extended plays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extended_play "Extended play"), and four [compilation albums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compilation_album "Compilation album"). After several line-up changes and self-made demos, they released their [self-titled EP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate_(EP) "Mercyful Fate (EP)") in 1982, with the line-up of [King Diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond "King Diamond") (vocals), Hank Shermann (lead and rhythm guitars), Michael Denner (rhythm and lead guitars), [Timi Hansen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timi_Hansen "Timi Hansen") (bass), and Kim Ruzz (drums). With this line-up, the group recorded its first two studio albums: 1983's _[Melissa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melissa\_(Mercyful\_Fate\_album) "Melissa (Mercyful Fate album)")_ and 1984's _[Don't Break the Oath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't\_Break\_the\_Oath "Don't Break the Oath")_. In spite of their reputation as one of the most acclaimed bands of the European heavy metal scene of the 1980s, Mercyful Fate was the subject of controversy due to their satanic imagery, and one of their songs "Into the Coven" (from _Melissa_) later gained notoriety for appearing as one of the [PMRC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parents_Music_Resource_Center "Parents Music Resource Center")'s "Filthy Fifteen" list of objectionable songs.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-PMRC-10)

After disbanding in 1985 due to musical differences, four out of the five members of Mercyful Fate reunited in 1992 and recorded the album _[In the Shadows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In\_the\_Shadows\_(album) "In the Shadows (album)")_, which was released the following year. During the 1990s, the band released four more studio albums and went through several line-up changes. Mercyful Fate went on hiatus in 1999, but had reunited on occasion during the 2000s. On August 1, 2019, it was announced that Mercyful Fate was reuniting on a more permanent basis, with plans to tour[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-shermann_bio-2)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-11) and release a new album, which will be their first since _[9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9\_(Mercyful\_Fate\_album) "9 (Mercyful Fate album)")_ in 1999.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Blabbermouth_album-12)

The staff of _[Loudwire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loudwire "Loudwire")_ named Mercyful Fate the 35th best metal band of all time.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-13)

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mercyful_Fate&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

### Formation and first releases (1981–1985)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mercyful_Fate&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Formation and first releases (1981–1985)")]

Mercyful Fate was originally formed in [Copenhagen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copenhagen "Copenhagen") in the spring of 1981,[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-14) following the dissolution of the band Brats.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Allmusic-15) Brats were a [punk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punk_rock "Punk rock")/[metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heavy_metal_music "Heavy metal music") band featuring future Mercyful Fate members [King Diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond "King Diamond") and guitarists [Hank Shermann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hank_Shermann "Hank Shermann") and Michael Denner.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Interview-16) After two studio albums and several line-up changes (including the addition of Diamond and the departure of Denner), Diamond and Shermann began writing new material that was much heavier than any of Brats' previous work.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Interview-16) The band's record label [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sony_Music "Sony Music") was not pleased with the material, and demanded they stop singing in English and become more commercial.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Interview-16) As a result, Diamond and Shermann quit the group and went on to form Mercyful Fate.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Interview-16) Former Rock Nalle bassist [Ole Beich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ole_Beich "Ole Beich") (later of [L.A. Guns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/L.A._Guns "L.A. Guns") and [Guns N' Roses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guns_N'_Roses "Guns N' Roses")) briefly joined the band around this time.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-17) After several line-up changes and semi-professional demo tapes, Mercyful Fate released their [self-titled EP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate_(EP) "Mercyful Fate (EP)") in 1982.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-szt-18)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Band_members-19) This line-up consisted of King Diamond, Hank Shermann, bassist [Timi Hansen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timi_Hansen "Timi Hansen"), drummer Kim Ruzz and guitarist Michael Denner.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-EP-20)

In July 1983, Mercyful Fate recorded their debut album at Easy Sound Recording in Copenhagen.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Melissa-21) Entitled _[Melissa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melissa\_(Mercyful\_Fate\_album) "Melissa (Mercyful Fate album)")_, the album was produced by Henrik Lund and released in October 1983 through [Roadrunner Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roadrunner_Records "Roadrunner Records").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Melissa-21)_Melissa_ has been referred to as "one of the first records to start to develop an '[extreme metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extreme_metal "Extreme metal")' sound" and was major influence on the then-emerging [thrash metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrash_metal "Thrash metal"), [death metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_metal "Death metal") and [black metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_metal "Black metal") genres.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-22) The character of Melissa, a [witch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Witchcraft "Witchcraft") who was burned at the stake, appears for the first time on the eponymous debut album and intermittently throughout the band's later work.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-23) One of the album's tracks, "Into the Coven", received particular attention two years later, when it was listed by the [Parents Music Resource Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parents_Music_Resource_Center "Parents Music Resource Center") (PMRC) as one of their "Filthy Fifteen" songs due to its perceived occult content.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-PMRC-10) King Diamond was, in reality, interested in [LaVeyan Satanism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LaVeyan_Satanism "LaVeyan Satanism"), which he called "a life philosophy" and stated that it had nothing to do with [the Devil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satan "Satan") of [Abrahamic religions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abrahamic_religions "Abrahamic religions").[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-24) After a number of concerts around Denmark, Mercyful Fate entered the studio in May 1984 to record their second studio album _[Don't Break the Oath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't\_Break\_the\_Oath "Don't Break the Oath")_, which was released on September 7, 1984.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Don't_Break_the_Oath-25) During the album's supporting tour, the band played the US for two months and made festival appearances in Germany.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-YouTube_#1-26) Despite winning a [cult following](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cult_following "Cult following") around the world, Mercyful Fate broke up in April 1985, due to musical differences.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Allmusic-15)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-YouTube_#1-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Music_Box-27) Guitarist Hank Shermann wanted the band to move to a more commercial sound;[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Allmusic-15) King Diamond refused and announced his departure from Mercyful Fate, which led to the band breaking up.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-YouTube_#1-26)

### After disbanding (1985–1992)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mercyful_Fate&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: After disbanding (1985–1992)")]

After Mercyful Fate broke up, King Diamond, along with Michael Denner and [Timi Hansen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timi_Hansen "Timi Hansen"), formed the eponymous [King Diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band) "King Diamond (band)") band.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-bandhistory02-28)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-YouTube_#1-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Music_Box-27) Both Denner and Hansen stayed with the group until 1987's _[Abigail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abigail\_(album) "Abigail (album)")_, after which both left King Diamond.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-King_Diamond_band_members-29) They were replaced by [Mike Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Moon_(musician) "Mike Moon (musician)") and Hal Patino, respectively, and King Diamond continued releasing albums even after Mercyful Fate had reformed.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-King_Diamond_band_members-29) After leaving King Diamond, Denner opened up a recordshop in Copenhagen, until 1988, when he formed the band Lavina (which would later become Zoser Mez), along with former bandmate Hank Shermann.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-King_Diamond_band_members-29)[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-YouTube_#2-30)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable\_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_] Hank Shermann had formed the hard rock band [Fate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fate_(band) "Fate (band)") in 1985, after having left Mercyful Fate.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Fate_Allmusic-31) With Fate, Shermann released two albums: 1985's _Fate_ and 1986's _[A Matter of Attitude](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Matter\_of\_Attitude "A Matter of Attitude")_.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Fate_Allmusic-31) After leaving the band, Shermann joined-up with Michael Denner to form Lavina.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Fate_Allmusic-31)

During the time Mercyful Fate were disbanded, Roadrunner Records released three Mercyful Fate [compilation albums](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compilation_album "Compilation album"). _[The Beginning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Beginning\_(Mercyful\_Fate\_album) "The Beginning (Mercyful Fate album)")_ was released on June 24, 1987, and featured material from the band's 1982 self-titled EP, as well as rare live and studio recordings.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-The_Beginning-32) On May 12, 1992, _[Return of the Vampire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Return\_of\_the\_Vampire "Return of the Vampire")_ was released, which was another compilation of rare studio recordings.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Return_of_the_Vampire-33) On October 6, 1992, Roadrunner Records released _[A Dangerous Meeting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A\_Dangerous\_Meeting "A Dangerous Meeting")_, a greatest hits album under the King Diamond name, featuring material from both Mercyful Fate and King Diamond.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-A_Dangerous_Meeting-34)

### Reunion (1992–1999)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mercyful_Fate&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Reunion (1992–1999)")]

In 1992, King Diamond, Hank Shermann, Michael Denner and Timi Hansen reunited to reform Mercyful Fate (drummer Kim Ruzz was replaced by Morten Nielsen).[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Band_members-19) The result was the band's third album _[In the Shadows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In\_the\_Shadows\_(album) "In the Shadows (album)")_, which was released on June 22, 1993 through [Metal Blade Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metal_Blade_Records "Metal Blade Records").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-In_the_Shadows-35) The album also featured a guest appearance by [Metallica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metallica "Metallica") drummer [Lars Ulrich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lars_Ulrich "Lars Ulrich") (a fellow Dane) on the track "Return of the Vampire".[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-In_the_Shadows-35) For the album's supporting tour, Morten Nielsen was replaced by King Diamond drummer [Snowy Shaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snowy_Shaw "Snowy Shaw"), due to a knee injury Nielsen had sustained.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Band_members-19) Bassist Timi Hansen was also replaced by [Sharlee D'Angelo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharlee_D'Angelo "Sharlee D'Angelo"), as Hansen did not want to take part in touring.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Band_members-19)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-About-36)[_[better source needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability#Questionable\_sources "Wikipedia:Verifiability")_] On June 27, 1994, the band released _[The Bell Witch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Bell\_Witch\_(EP) "The Bell Witch (EP)")_, an EP of live tracks, as well as studio recordings from _In the Shadows_.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-The_Bell_Witch-37)

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/0d/King_Diamond_live_1999.jpg/250px-King_Diamond_live_1999.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:King_Diamond_live_1999.jpg)

[King Diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond "King Diamond") performing with Mercyful Fate in 1999

On October 25, 1994, Mercyful Fate released its fourth album _[Time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time\_(Mercyful\_Fate\_album) "Time (Mercyful Fate album)")_, which was recorded and mixed at the Dallas Sound Lab during May and August of that year.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Time-38) After the album's release, drummer Snowy Shaw was replaced by Bjarne T. Holm for the Time Tour.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Band_members-19) Holm had originally been asked to join Mercyful Fate back in 1981, but had declined due to prior commitments.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Band_members-19) The band spent January through February 1996 recording and mixing their next album _[Into the Unknown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Into\_the\_Unknown\_(Mercyful\_Fate\_album) "Into the Unknown (Mercyful Fate album)")_, which was released on August 20, 1996.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Into_the_Unknown-39) After the album's release, guitarist Michael Denner left the band and was replaced by [Mike Wead](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mike_Wead "Mike Wead").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Band_members-19) In October 1997, Mercyful Fate began recording its sixth album _[Dead Again](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dead\_Again\_(Mercyful\_Fate\_album) "Dead Again (Mercyful Fate album)")_ at the Nomad Recording Studio in [Carrollton, Texas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carrollton,_Texas "Carrollton, Texas").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Dead_Again-40)_Dead Again_ was released on June 9, 1998.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Dead_Again-40) In February 1999, Mercyful Fate began recording its seventh studio album _[9](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/9\_(Mercyful\_Fate\_album) "9 (Mercyful Fate album)")_, which was released on June 15, 1999.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Nine-41)

### Hiatus and sporadic reunions (1999–2018)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mercyful_Fate&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Hiatus and sporadic reunions (1999–2018)")]

After the supporting tour for _9_, which included dates in North America, South America and supporting Metallica on a European tour, Mercyful Fate was put on hiatus.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-:0-42) King Diamond focused on his eponymous band, along with guitarist Mike Wead, who joined the group during the European _[House of God](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/House\_of\_God\_(album) "House of God (album)")_ tour.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-King_Diamond_band_members-29) Hank Shermann and Bjarne T. Holm reunited with Michael Denner to form Force of Evil, while Sharlee D'Angelo joined the band [Arch Enemy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arch_Enemy "Arch Enemy").[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Force_of_Evil-43) When asked about the current state of the band in 2008, Diamond stated that Mercyful Fate had been "hibernating", and that " they were "definitely not finished, at least in my book."[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-44) In August 2008, King Diamond was asked by Metallica drummer [Lars Ulrich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lars_Ulrich "Lars Ulrich") if Mercyful Fate would be willing to participate in [Activision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Activision "Activision")'s _[Guitar Hero: Metallica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guitar\_Hero:\_Metallica "Guitar Hero: Metallica")_ video game.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Guitar_Hero-45) Ulrich requested the original masters for two of the band's songs, so they could be used in the game.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Guitar_Hero-45) Unable to locate them, Diamond suggested to Activision the band re-record the songs, and as a result, King Diamond, Hank Shermann, Michael Denner, Timi Hansen and Bjarne T. Holm reunited to re-record the songs "Evil" and "Curse of the Pharaohs".[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Guitar_Hero-45) King Diamond was also made into a playable character in the game.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Guitar_Hero-45)

On December 7, 2011, King Diamond, Hank Shermann, Michael Denner and Timi Hansen reunited onstage at Metallica's 30th Anniversary concert at [the Fillmore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Fillmore "The Fillmore") in [San Francisco, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Francisco,_California "San Francisco, California"), where they, alongside Metallica, performed the latter's "Mercyful Fate" medley from _[Garage Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Garage\_Inc. "Garage Inc.")_[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-GWorld-46)

On January 28, 2017, the original line-up of Mercyful Fate (minus Diamond) reunited to receive the Pioneer Prize at the [Steppeulven](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steppeulven "Steppeulven") ceremony by the Danish Association of Music Critics at the [Bremen Teater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bremen_Teater_(Copenhagen) "Bremen Teater (Copenhagen)") in Copenhagen. This was the first time that drummer Kim Ruzz appeared with the band since the 1985 split.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-47)

### Full-time reunion (2019–present)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mercyful_Fate&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Full-time reunion (2019–present)")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e5/Mercyful_Fate_%2852202517675%29.jpg/250px-Mercyful_Fate_%2852202517675%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Mercyful_Fate_(52202517675).jpg)

Mercyful Fate performing in 2022

On August 1, 2019, it was announced that Mercyful Fate would be performing an unspecified number of concerts throughout Europe in the summer of 2020. The band's line-up consists of King Diamond on vocals, Hank Shermann on guitar, Bjarne T. Holm on drums, Mike Wead on guitar and [Joey Vera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joey_Vera "Joey Vera") on bass, the latter of whom was filling in for Timi Hansen, who was battling cancer;[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-48) Vera then became their full-time bass player after Hansen died on November 4, 2019, shortly after his 61st birthday.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-49) Aside from previously released material, the band was also going to perform new songs over the course of the summer.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-50)

In a May 2020 interview with Heavy magazine, Shermann said that he had "written six or seven songs" for the band's new album.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-51) On June 2, 2022, Mercyful Fate performed their first live show since 1999 in [Hanover](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hanover "Hanover") as part of a European tour, where they debuted a brand new song titled "The Jackal of Salzburg".[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-52)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-53) In the fall of that year, they embarked on their first North American tour in two decades supported by [Kreator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kreator "Kreator") and [Midnight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midnight_(band) "Midnight (band)").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-:0-42)

On January 16, 2024, Mercyful Fate announced that they had "mutually decided to split ways" with Vera.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-54) Three days later, it was announced Becky Baldwin was the new bassist of the band, who filled in for Vera during the band's 2022 tour.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-55) In the following month, Baldwin stated that the new Mercyful Fate album was not expected to be released before 2025, due to [King Diamond](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond "King Diamond")'s focus on his [namesake band](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Diamond_(band) "King Diamond (band)")'s upcoming thirteenth studio album _Saint Lucifer's Hospital 1920_ (formerly titled _The Institute_).[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-57)

Mercyful Fate is set to play their first shows in three years in the summer of 2027 at Spain's Leyendas Del Rock and the UK's [Bloodstock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bloodstock_Open_Air "Bloodstock Open Air") festivals, and King Diamond has hinted that their new album will be released to coincide with those dates.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-58)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-59)[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-60)

## Artistry

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mercyful_Fate&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Artistry")]

### Musical style

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mercyful_Fate&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Musical style")]

Mercyful Fate was a part of the [first wave of black metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First-wave_black_metal "First-wave black metal"), along with other groups, such as [Venom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venom_(band) "Venom (band)"), [Bathory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bathory_(band) "Bathory (band)"), and [Hellhammer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hellhammer "Hellhammer").[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-sam-61) Many of these groups helped establish the style upon which future black metal artists would later build.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-sam-61) Unlike the other first-wave bands, typical elements of Mercyful Fate's style are influences from [progressive rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_rock "Progressive rock"),[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-rhi1-62) epic 1970s [hard rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hard_rock "Hard rock"),[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-szt-18) and traditional heavy metal. As many of the band's songs featured lyrics about [Satanism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satanism "Satanism") and the [occult](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occult "Occult")[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Melissa_Review-9)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Don't_Break_the_Oath_Review-63) and King Diamond was among the first black metal musicians to use the now famous [corpse paint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corpse_paint "Corpse paint"),[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-metalstrom-64) Mercyful Fate was a pioneer in developing black metal,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Melissa_Review-9)[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-Don't_Break_the_Oath_Review-63) although their musical style was not as much an influence as that of other first wave bands.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-szt-18)

According to Jeff Kitts of _[Guitar World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guitar\_World "Guitar World")_, "Mercyful Fate, along with Venom, set the parameters for black metal in the early eighties", and he claimed that the band's [self-titled EP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate_(EP) "Mercyful Fate (EP)") and their first two albums, _[Melissa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melissa\_(Mercyful\_Fate\_album) "Melissa (Mercyful Fate album)")_ and _[Don't Break the Oath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don't\_Break\_the\_Oath "Don't Break the Oath")_, all "established a heavy, [Sabbath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Sabbath "Black Sabbath")-influenced sound topped with the schizophrenic vocals of the goulishly made-up King Diamond, whose lyrics were more explicitly Satanic than anything that had come before."[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-65)

### Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Mercyful_Fate&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Legacy")]

Regarded as one of the pioneers of [extreme metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extreme_metal "Extreme metal"), Mercyful Fate has been cited as influential to genres including [black metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_metal "Black metal"), [death metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_metal "Death metal"), and [thrash metal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrash_metal "Thrash metal"). They have been cited as an influence on or inspiration to bands of the then-emerging death metal genre, including [Death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death_(metal_band) "Death (metal band)"),[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-66)[Morbid Angel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morbid_Angel "Morbid Angel"),[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-67)[Obituary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Obituary_(band) "Obituary (band)"),[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-68)[Carcass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carcass_(band) "Carcass (band)"),[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-givememetal-69)[Cannibal Corpse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannibal_Corpse "Cannibal Corpse"),[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-70) and [Incantation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incantation_(American_band) "Incantation (American band)").[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate#cite_note-givememetal-69)

**Fate** is a Danish rock band originally formed in 1984. They released four albums between 1984 and 1990 before disbanding in 1993. However, after a one-off reunion at a German music festival in 2004, Fate was reformed and released a new album, _V_, in 2006. In 2010, the band released _Best of Fate 25 Years_ on EMI and, in November 2011, the album _Ghosts from the Past_ was released on AOR Heaven in EU and Rubicon in Japan.

## History

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Fate_(band)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: History")]

The band Fate formed when former [Mercyful Fate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercyful_Fate "Mercyful Fate") guitarist Hank Shermann (René Krolmark), Maxim Reality singer Jeff "Lox" Limbo (Jens Meinert), bass / keyboard player Pete Steiner (Peter Steincke) and drummer Bob Lance (Bjarne Holm),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fate_(band)#cite_note-LarkinHR-1) met with producer Simon Hanhart. The band recorded _[Cruisin' for a Bruisin'](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cruisin'\_for\_a\_Bruisin'\_(Fate\_album) "Cruisin' for a Bruisin' (Fate album)")_ in 1988,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fate_(band)#cite_note-LarkinHR-1) which featured the single "Lovers" (released as a single plus videoclip in 1988) and a new version of "Love on the Rox" from the band's debut.

**King Diamond** es el nombre artístico del músico danés **Kim Bendix Petersen** (nacido en [Copenhague](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Copenhague "Copenhague"), el 14 de junio de 1956). King Diamond también es el nombre de su proyecto musical más conocido. En este proyecto, él es el cantante principal y el compositor. La revista _Hit Parader_ lo incluyó en su lista de los 100 mejores vocalistas de metal del mundo.

## King Diamond: Un Músico Único

King Diamond es conocido por su estilo musical y su puesta en escena. Ha creado una carrera destacada en el mundo del [heavy metal](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Heavy_metal "Heavy metal"). Su música y sus presentaciones en vivo son muy especiales.

### Inicios y Proyectos Musicales

King Diamond comenzó su carrera musical con la banda Black Rose en 1979. Esta banda tenía influencias del [rock psicodélico](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Rock_psicod%C3%A9lico "Rock psicodélico") y el [hard rock](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Hard_rock "Hard rock").

En 1981, formó la banda Mercyful Fate. Este fue su primer gran proyecto. En Mercyful Fate, mezcló un estilo de heavy metal complejo con letras que exploraban temas oscuros.

Finalmente, en 1985, creó su proyecto solista llamado King Diamond. Este proyecto ha estado activo desde entonces. También participó en otras bandas como Brats y Danger Zone. En 2004, colaboró con [Dave Grohl](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Dave_Grohl "Dave Grohl") en la canción "Sweet Dreams" para el álbum _Probot_.

### Su Carrera como Solista

Como solista, King Diamond desarrolló un sonido más teatral y progresivo. Mantuvo la energía y los cambios de ritmo de Mercyful Fate. En sus álbumes, King Diamond suele contar historias de horror que él mismo escribe.

Sus álbumes son a menudo álbumes conceptuales. Esto significa que todas las canciones cuentan una misma historia. La historia del álbum _Abigail_ es una de las más famosas. Este álbum es muy querido por sus seguidores y ha recibido excelentes críticas.

#### El Estilo Musical y Vocal

La voz de King Diamond es muy particular. Usa cambios repentinos en el tono y a menudo canta en [falsete](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Falsete "Falsete"). Su maquillaje llamativo y sus historias lo hacen único.

Aunque su falsete es muy conocido, King Diamond tiene una técnica vocal muy amplia. Puede usar diferentes tipos de voz y transmitir muchas emociones. Esto se nota tanto en sus grabaciones como en sus conciertos.

La colaboración de Andy LaRocque ha sido muy importante para el sonido de King Diamond. Andy es el guitarrista y ha ayudado a escribir muchas canciones. Sus solos y [riffs](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Riff "Riff") (melodías de guitarra) son una parte clave del sonido de la banda. Andy LaRocque es el único miembro original que ha estado con King Diamond desde 1985.

#### La Puesta en Escena

King Diamond es famoso por sus presentaciones en vivo. En ellas, representa las historias de horror de sus álbumes. Es como ver una obra de teatro con música.

Actualmente, la banda cuenta con una actriz, Jody Cachia. Ella interpreta a diferentes personajes de las historias de King Diamond en los conciertos. Esto hace que los shows sean aún más especiales y envolventes.

### Su Maquillaje Característico

[![Image 5: Archivo:Tuska 20130628 - King Diamond - 05](https://ninos.kiddle.co/images/thumb/b/b5/Tuska_20130628_-_King_Diamond_-_05.jpg/200px-Tuska_20130628_-_King_Diamond_-_05.jpg)](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Archivo:Tuska_20130628_-_King_Diamond_-_05.jpg)

[](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Archivo:Tuska_20130628_-_King_Diamond_-_05.jpg "Aumentar")

 King Diamond en una presentación en el Tuska Open Air Metal Festival (2013).

Desde sus inicios con Mercyful Fate, King Diamond ha usado un maquillaje facial muy distintivo, conocido como _corpsepaint_. Ha cambiado su estilo de maquillaje varias veces a lo largo de su carrera. Él ha mencionado que se inspiró en el maquillaje que usaba [Alice Cooper](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Alice_Cooper "Alice Cooper") en el escenario.

Al principio de los años ochenta, King Diamond recibió una carta de [Gene Simmons](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Gene_Simmons "Gene Simmons") de la banda [Kiss](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Kiss "Kiss"). En la carta, se le acusaba de haber copiado su maquillaje. Aunque no hubo una demanda formal, King Diamond decidió cambiar su estilo. Poco después, apareció con un maquillaje diferente y más original.

### Influencia en la Música

King Diamond ha ganado muchos seguidores en el mundo del metal. Ha influido en bandas muy populares como [Metallica](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Metallica "Metallica"). Su impacto se sintió primero en los países escandinavos y luego en Estados Unidos y Europa.

Desde el lanzamiento del álbum _Melissa_ de Mercyful Fate en 1983, King Diamond es considerado un artista de culto. Algunos lo ven como un pionero del black metal, aunque esto es un tema de debate. Su sonido es más cercano al heavy metal tradicional y al speed metal. Sin embargo, sus letras y su estilo oscuro han sido una inspiración para muchas bandas.

King Diamond es un gran admirador de la banda Uriah Heep. La canción "The Wizard" de Uriah Heep se usa como introducción en sus conciertos de _Abigail_. En honor al vocalista de Uriah Heep, David Byron, su hijo se llama Byron.

### Vida Personal

Kim Bendix Petersen está casado con Livia Zita, una cantante de origen húngaro. La pareja vive en [Dallas](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Dallas "Dallas"), [Texas](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Texas "Texas"), [Estados Unidos](https://ninos.kiddle.co/Estados_Unidos "Estados Unidos").

Livia Zita ha participado como vocalista de apoyo en los álbumes _The Puppet Master_ y _Give Me Your Soul...Please_. También ha cantado en sus conciertos en vivo.

Además, Livia es su socia en los negocios musicales. Trabaja con él para organizar material antiguo de King Diamond y Mercyful Fate para futuros lanzamientos en DVD. También ha colaborado en la remasterización de varios de sus discos. En 2018, Livia y Kim tuvieron a su primer hijo, a quien llamaron Byron.
